main_text.head: DE IVDICIIS VRINARVM TRACTATVS, EX probatis collectus authoribus, & in tabulae formam confectus.

p.i: CVM tres genere facultates in tribus existant principijs, cerebro, corde, & hepate: ex singulorum functionibus, tum imbecillitas tum robur dignoscuntur. Cerebri quidem memoria & ratiocinatione, & subseruientibus alijs arbitrarijs functionibus. Cordis, per arteriarum motus. Hepatis verò facultas, cuiusnam roboris vel imbecillitatis fuerit: hæc quidem quæ in ventre est, per ea quæ subeunt & subducuntur, agnoscitur: illa vero quæ in hepate & venis est, per vrinas. Sunt siquidem in huiusmodi vrinis signa euidentissima, alia siquidem exquisitæ concoctionis, alia diminutæ, alia verò prorsus abolitæ, veluti & in ventre contingit. Præterea et vt in ventre externa quædam pariter excernuntur

page.notes: The initial C is a woodcut historiated letter and is transcribed as "CVM" with the C joined to the word. The first line of the body reads "VM tres genere facultates in" with the initial C from the woodcut. Some letters in the body are faint; "hepate" and "vrinis" read as printed. The last line "cernuntur" is set flush right.
